input.query: Do the authors of 'Mapping Languages and Demographics with Georeferenced Corpora' offer a hypothesis for why Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country?

claims.text: The paper states that Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country.
In the discussion, the authors state that in countries where corpora do not represent all languages produced by local populations, Twitter has fewer missing languages.

The authors note that English and Spanish are very common on Twitter, so countries predominantly using these languages have good representation by default, which is one factor disguised in the results.

Regarding why Twitter and web-crawled data diverge in representing populations, the authors hypothesize that Twitter represents wealthier populations, and offer an alternate interpretation that their Twitter collection is based on urban areas with wealthier populations.

The supplied evidence does not present an explicit, dedicated hypothesis specifically explaining why Twitter data better predicts the language inventory; the discussion attributes differences to coverage factors such as commonness of English/Spanish and fewer missing languages.
